approaches.name: social registry MIS with API interoperability and hazard-data targeting
approaches.description: A management information system holds socio-economic data on about 10 million people, shared via secure APIs and overlaid with flood models for targeting. Practices: RSU social registry MIS for multi-program targeting; Flood hazard mapping overlaying RSU data with FATHOM risk models; coverage diagnostic mapping underserved areas for RSU expansion; API interoperability between RSU MIS and social program systems; API-based secure data exchange between RSU MIS and social program systems; RSU-MIS registry of rural household socio-economic data via outreach.

evidence.text: The RSU Management Information System (MIS) is now fully operational and contains socio-economic data of about 1.7 million households (close to 10 million individuals) as of June 2026.

extra_evidence.text: Eight programs use the RSU for targeting.

A large survey drive in 1,000 villages and a campaign in urban areas were completed in early September 2026; the information is being processed and the operation is expected to result in 2.1 million households registered by December 2026 (PDO-level indicator target), supported by 1,200 trained professionals across 31 regions and an expanded network of 354 fixed registration points (guichets) for on-demand registration.

In conjunction to the implementation of the PforR, as part of the Bank’s technical assistance, a flood hazard mapping exercise – overlaying RSU household data with FATHOM risk models – was conducted in the Cavally region to showcase the potential of geographic targeting.

Using a coverage diagnostic, sous-préfectures where the poverty-to-enrollment ratio is 2 or higher are flagged as underserved, and settlements exceeding 10,000 inhabitants without an existing guichet are identified as priority sites.

This approach is expected to result in a focus in several areas in regions such as Guémon, San-Pédro, and Moronou, with updated maps and indices to be integrated into the RSU operations manual ahead of each expansion drive.

approaches.name: digital cash transfers and mobile-wallet savings for poor households
approaches.description: Digital payments and savings accounts via mobile operators, with literacy training and operator-data verification, replace cash-based transfers and savings for beneficiaries. Practices: Pre-protocol digital cash transfers for flood-affected households; Multi-operator G2P payment mechanism with beneficiary provider choice; remunerated digital savings accounts with literacy training and nudges; piloted digital savings model scaled up for PTMP beneficiaries; digital savings accounts scale-up via mobile wallets; digital financial inclusion pilot with rigorous evaluation and scale-up roadmap; trigger-based digital cash transfers to flood-affected households; mobile-operator data verification of digital account ownership; TrésorPay/TrésorMoney government payment platform assessment.
approaches.why_innovative: New process: pre-agreed shock-triggered digital payouts - cue: 'pilot' | category Financial; adoption apply; judged in 1 round(s); final check: digital core, in_use before 2019

evidence.text: Shock response framework defined and operationalized, with tangible results achieved including a pilot providing digital cash transfers, according to preestablished protocols, to 1,731 poor households affected by flooding in the Cavally region – demonstrating the Program's operational readiness to respond rapidly to covariate shocks.

extra_evidence.text: The operational protocol and manual were designed, and the mechanism was successfully piloted in 2024.
On payment systems, the AF will continue supporting the transition toward a multi-operator G2P payment mechanism and towards introducing beneficiary choice among payment providers.
The dynamics among operators in the mobile payments sector in Côte d’Ivoire makes beneficiaries choice possible.

To this end, the AF will support a structured package combining access to remunerated digital savings accounts with financial and digital literacy training, CAC accompaniment, behavioral nudges, and peer-learning mechanisms.

The World Bank First Additional Financing to the Côte d'Ivoire Productive Social Safety Nets System Strengthening Program (P175594) Page 12 Official Use Only services – strengthening financial and digital literacy and expanding the adoption of digital savings practices improving pathways to credit eligibility and households' capacity to build financial buffers against shocks.

Early results from the pilot – launched in March 2026 across four regions, 80 localities, and 2,000 PTMP beneficiaries45 – are highly encouraging: ownership of digital savings accounts increased more than tenfold (from approximately 3 percent to 34 percent among participants), average end-of-month savings balances increased more than eightfold, and gender-disaggregated data shows particularly strong effects for women, including up to four times greater growth in digital savings account ownership compared to men.

Building on these results, the AF will support the progressive scale-up of the model, retaining the components demonstrating the strongest behavioral impact while continuing to assess cost-effectiveness ahead of full rollout.

These are designed to move beneficiaries progressively from cash-in/cash-out use of mobile money toward active and sustained use of digital savings and, eventually, broader formal financial products including credit.
The AF scales up a digital financial inclusion intervention grounded in both global evidence and PTMP-specific research.

Moreover, early pilot results provide tangible evidence of impact, particularly for women, informing the design of the AF-supported scale-up, including a tenfold increase in digital savings account ownership and a twofold reduction in cash-in/cash-out behavior.

The Program’s desk review found that, while AVECs are effective at building savings habits and women's economic empowerment, they have greater long-term impact when combined with access to formal digital financial services.

USD 3,500,000 upon timely implementation and completion of response through digital cash transfers to affected households, in accordance to the shock response operations manual Description Data source/ Agency BCPFS, with inputs from DGSAH and DG Observatoire (MCNSLP) Verification Entity IVA Procedure The IVA will verify: (i) whether the Ministry triggered the response to a flood, based on the official trigger notification, as per Shock response operations manual;

(iii) whether digital cash transfers were disbursed to all identified and targeted affected households no more than 30 days from the triggered response mechanism, as evidenced by payment records in the MIS; and (iv) if the payment covered at least 1,000 households.
To confirm ownership and use of digital saving or credit accounts, the IVA will wherever faeasibile verify data from the mobile operator.

Should data from operators not be made available, the IVA will verify the result through a survey with a random sample of participants, and either view or receive declarative information on ownership and use.
In addition, the IVA will conduct a survey of a representative sample of beneficiaries to verify their participation in training sessions and their active use of mobile financial service.

The AF will continuously evaluate options as the digital payments landscape diversifies – including the potential of the government's TrésorPay/TrésorMoney platform as its interoperability and agent network mature – and will use the IPF component to support continuous technical engagement.
